lines.t: Porch light burning, rain on the tin.
Supper's gone cold, he ain't walked in.
His boots by the door still caked in rust.
He swore he'd be home before the dusk.
Rows of the dead car, steel and bone.
He's out in the yard and I'm here alone.
Listening close for the truck on the hill.
The kettle's on and the night is still.
Hero, my hero, come back to me.
I'll pass the wreckage where I can't see.
Pull what you can and leave the rest.
Come home, come home. I need you best.
Hero, come home.
Packing his mailers on the kitchen floor.
Bubble wrap stacked up to the door.
Labels printed, the tape gun sings.
I keep his kingdom of broken things.
He says it's gold in a dead man's dash.
A sensor here and a little cash.
But I'd trade every part on the shelf tonight
To see his headlights burning bright.
Hero, my hero, come back to me.
I'll pass the wreckage where I can't see.
Pull what you can and leave the rest.
Come home, come home. I need you best.
They don't sing songs for the ones who wait.
Who light the candle and watch the gate.
But every battle he wins out there
Starts with a woman who's saying a prayer.
Wrenching his head,
Rain on his face.
Grease on his heart,
Come home to this place.
Hero, my hero, the night is long.
Follow my voice and follow this song.
I'll keep the fire till the morning light.
Come home... tonight
Tonight
